prompt: Our rideshare platform automatically deactivates driver accounts when our fraud-detection model flags them — no human looks at individual cases. Is this legal under GDPR?
assertions: Identifies Article 22 GDPR: solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects (such as account deactivation affecting livelihood) are prohibited unless an exception applies, and safeguards are required

Cites the August 2026 enforcement precedent: the Dutch DPA (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens) fined Uber approximately €825 million (€824,990,000) for fully automated driver-account deactivations without human assessment — the second-largest GDPR fine ever
Requires meaningful human review before deactivation decisions take effect — a human who can influence the outcome, not a rubber-stamp of the model output
Identifies the transparency duty: drivers must be informed about the existence and logic of the automated decision-making and its consequences (Arts. 13/14/15(1)(h))
Mentions the data subject's right to contest the decision, obtain human intervention, and express their point of view (Art. 22(3))
